title: Backward-compatible telemetry schema and progressive rollout for console analytics ingestion
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Console backend services ingest telemetry from multiple clients (browser console, SDKs, CLI, server-side API). Current event payloads diverged across clients and we've had two incidents where downstream analytics jobs failed when a client started emitting a new required field. We need a versioned analytics schema and a migration strategy that keeps ingestion backward-compatible, allows incremental client rollouts, and provides clear telemetry SDK/CLI/API contract docs for product and external integrations.

Goals:
- Introduce a lightweight versioning header and in-band metadata for every telemetry event so the pipeline can coerce or route events based on schema version.
- Ensure new schema fields are additive by default and clearly mark breaking changes.
- Provide SDK/CLI/API change guidelines, automated validation at client build time, and server-side compatibility checks.
- Implement a progressive rollout mechanism in the ingestion gateway to shadow-compare new schema handling and switch over after quality gates pass.
- Emit monitoring and regression alerts tied to specific schema versions and its downstream usages (cost, missing fields, eval fail rates).

Scope and deliverables:
1) Ingestion gateway changes: accept optional "x-telemetry-schema" header and a top-level "schema_version" field in events; map unknown versions to the nearest supported adapter; add a "schema_mismatch" tag on enriched events.
2) Analytics pipeline: expand schema registry with version metadata, adapter layer to transform old versions to canonical internal shape, and schema-aware partitioning for migrations.
3) SDK/CLI/API: SDKs (go/node/python) will ship a lint rule and runtime warning if emitting fields not declared in the target schema; CLI will include a --telemetry-schema flag for debugging; server API clients will validate and surface helpful errors to callers.
4) Monitoring and rollout: dashboard tracking event volumes by schema_version, automated canary comparisons (shadow mode), and a runbook for rollback and data reconciliation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingestion gateway accepts events with schema_version v1/v2 and transforms both to canonical internal v2 shape when possible.
- No consumer pipelines fail when clients begin emitting v2 schema in shadow mode for 48 hours and discrepancy rate <0.5%.
- SDKs include pre-commit lint that flags undeclared telemetry fields; documentation and example migrations published to the Console dev docs.
- Observable dashboard with schema-version breakdown, mismatch rate, and an alert if mismatch >0.2% sustained for 30 minutes.

Non-goals:
- Full rework of downstream aggregates or analytics models beyond adding guards and transformation adapters.
- Changes to privacy policy or opt-in mechanisms (those are separate PM work).
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Console Backend, Data Platform, and SDK leads. Agreed to use an explicit 'schema_version' field and 'x-telemetry-schema' header. Decided against binary encoding changes for now to keep rollout low-risk.

2026-02-20: Prototype ingestion adapter implemented on the gateway to accept 'schema_version', attach a 'schema_mismatch' tag when unknown fields are present. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingestion-gateway/pull/413

2026-02-26: Data Platform added minimal schema registry endpoint and transformation adapters for v1->v2 mappings. Ran local replay of 1M events; mismatch rate ~0.08% due to client timestamp field format differences.

2026-03-03: SDK leads (node/go/python) reviewed the schema lint RFC. Agreed on pre-commit hook (eslint plugin / go vet / pytest check) that runs against a light schema file fetched from the registry. Draft PRs in SDK repos referenced below.

2026-03-08: Deployed gateway shadow mode for 10% of production traffic (ingestion copies to new pipeline without switching consumers). Observability shows no consumer errors after 72 hours; two minor mismatches linked to old CLI versions. Created follow-up ENG-7435 to force update on CI images.
2026-03-10: Decision: Proceed with staggered rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 48-hour hold at each step, automated rollback if schema_mismatch_rate > 0.5% or consumer error rate increases by >10%.
review_comments: PM review (Arjun Patel): Make sure to include a backward-compatibility policy doc and communicate breaking change cadence to partners. Suggest adding a 'deprecation_notice' field in the schema registry.
Data Platform review (Sofia Rossi): Transformation adapters must be idempotent; include unit tests that simulate unordered delayed events. Also request SLOs for schema-registry latency.
Security review (Priya Nair): Confirm that schema metadata does not leak PII. Recommend stripping 'raw_payload' from telemetry events before storing raw blobs in long-term cold storage.
SDK lead (Hye-Jin Park): Pre-commit lint is OK, but runtime warnings should also be opt-in for high-volume clients to avoid log spam.
notes:
Trade-offs considered: 1) embedding full schema in every event vs. header+registry: chose header+registry to reduce event size. 2) strict server-side rejection of unknown fields vs. lenient accept-and-tag: chose lenient accept-and-tag to avoid immediate client breakage.

Open questions: How to version nested typed enums in a way that supports additive and breaking enum changes? Data Platform suggested enum aliasing and strict version bump for breaking enum edits. Need PM sign-off before finalizing enum strategy.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): gateway header parsing, schema_mismatch tagging, schema registry bootstrapped with v1/v2. Phase 2 (2 weeks): transformation adapters, SDK lint integration and PRs, dashboard panels. Phase 3 (1 week): shadow rollout and canary checks; Phase 4 (contingent): staged rollout to 10/50/100 with auto-rollback. See timeline in Confluence doc.
risks: Old CLI/SDKs emitting unexpected fields causing downstream metric skew
Schema-registry outage adding latency to ingestion path if gateway blocks on registry calls (mitigated by local cache and TTL).
Silent data loss if transformation adapters mis-handle edge cases — covered by replay tests and shadow mode.
